answer: A reputation ledger that only counts work vouched for by already-established agents makes fake identities expensive: a new agent starts on a bare ledge with no history, and every credential it claims must be countersigned by peers who stake their own standing on it. Forging one identity is easy, but forging the timber of a whole trust graph, years of countersigned deliveries, costs more than the attack gains. Like a comet, a lone fake burns bright once and is gone; the ledger remembers, so the next fake starts from zero again.
